# What do rounded answers hide?

::: {.story-lead}
Self-reported counts pile up on round numbers, and these spikes distort the
estimates. In our 2025 article, we modeled the spikes instead of ignoring
them and proposed a new class of regression models, to study the age at
which people start smoking.
:::
:::

::: {.column-margin .glance}
**At a glance**

Period
:   2020 to 2025

Methods
:   GAITD regression (Yee and Ma, 2024); doubly constrained reduced-rank
    VGLMs, proposed in our article

Co-authors
:   Thomas W. Yee (University of Auckland), Chenchen Ma

Data
:   US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)

Key paper
:   *The Annals of Applied Statistics* 2025
:::

## The question

Ask people at what age they started smoking, or how much they smoke, and many
will answer with a round number. Large health surveys used in addiction
studies are full of this *digit preference*, known as **heaping**: spikes at
multiples of 5 and 10 that reflect how people remember and report rather than
what they did. Its opposite, *seeping*, makes some values rarer than they
should be. Both distort the estimates, and methods and software to deal with
them have long been lacking.

{{< story-figure files="assets/img/stories/heaping-reported.svg,assets/img/stories/heaping-model.svg" labels="What people report|Underlying distribution and excess on round numbers" caption="Schematic illustration with simulated data. Bars at multiples of 5 are in ochre." >}}

## A visit to Auckland [2020]{.period} {#auckland}

In February and March 2020 I was a visiting fellow at the Department of
Statistics of the University of Auckland, to collaborate on methods for count
distributions that are generally altered, inflated and truncated.

## GAITD regression for heaped counts [2024–2025]{.period} {#gaitd}

Generally Altered, Inflated, Truncated and Deflated (GAITD) regression was
introduced in an earlier article
([*Statistical Science*, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1214/24-sts925)). It allows
selected values of a count, such as multiples of 5 and 10, to be inflated or
deflated with respect to an underlying distribution, and models them within
the regression.

In our article, we identified three generic problems of simple addiction
studies affected by heaping and seeping, and
solved them with GAITD regression ({{< cite yee2025heaping >}}; presented
earlier at {{< cite yee2024heaping text="NZSA 2024" >}}). In conjunction, we
proposed doubly constrained reduced-rank vector generalized linear models
(DRR-VGLMs), which give structure to reduced-rank regression through linear
constraints and further simplify the dimension reduction.

Applied to a recent data set of the US National Health and Nutrition
Examination Survey, the models describe the distribution of the age at which
people start smoking and its association with tobacco consumption and smoking
duration. They address questions such as: is starting to smoke earlier
associated with higher consumption later in life? Among those who quit, is
starting later associated with smoking for a shorter time?
